findings.title: The repaired orbit-review sentence says the requirement restates no pointer value, while its own scenario states one
findings.recommendation: Walk 1's fix reads `this requirement names it and restates neither its values nor its per-mode split`, but the same requirement's `Spine fields carry deterministic facts under persist-first` scenario names the change-mode value `/orbit:address-reviews <change>` (correctly: a scenario is a test case and names its expected output). Narrow the clause to `this paragraph names it and restates neither …`, or drop `restates neither its values nor its per-mode split` and keep the pointer alone.

findings.title: D6 says the apply chunk keys are written as null when unused, but chunk_complete is a boolean
findings.recommendation: `ApplyComputed` (src/core/emit-composition.ts:1387-1398) types `chunk`, `chunk_name`, `files_touched` and `diff_base` as nullable and `chunk_complete` as `boolean`. The argument holds — every key is written on every apply emit — so reword to `on every apply emit (the nullable ones as null when unused)` or drop the parenthetical.

walk_entry.title: Two stated counts disagree with measurement (182 self-pointer emits; 35 delta scenarios)

commentary: A verification of the two walk logs over their sweep scopes. The residual check from the external return's commit (c79807ca) lists six files, all inside the walks' edit records. Every regression is the same shape: a walk sentence asserting a fact one notch broader than what it checked — a copied count, a type stated for a set of fields, a scope word ('requirement') wider than the paragraph it governs. Two were caught only by executing the claim (the count with the renderer's own predicate, the field types from ApplyComputed); a read would have passed both. No design decision moved: every regression is a wording repair at the site the walk already edited.
